feature: Kill default return True in _evaluate_behavioral(); require explicit handling for all criteria
problem: Line 953 of session_judge.py returns True for any unrecognized criterion text, silently passing unmatched behavioral checks. 34 of 87 behavioral criteria strings across 28 scenarios currently fall through to this default. This hides rubric drift and makes eval scores unreliable.
proposed_solution: Phase approach: (1) Audit all behavioral criteria strings across scenarios to identify the 34 fallthroughs, (2) Add branches or generalize existing branches to cover all 34, (3) Replace return True with UNMATCHED sentinel, (4) Update check_behavioral and judge_session to handle UNMATCHED, (5) Update session_report to count UNMATCHED separately. Gap-26 branch merges deferred to separate task.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: _evaluate_behavioral() last line returns a sentinel value (not True) that maps to UNMATCHED verdict
AC2: Unmatched behavioral criteria produce result 'UNMATCHED' in the judgment output — never PASS, UNCERTAIN, or UNKNOWN
AC3: A structured warning is included in the result dict (key: 'warning') identifying the unmatched criterion text
AC4: check_behavioral() maps the UNMATCHED sentinel to result: 'UNMATCHED' with tier: 'structural'
AC5: judge_session() summary exposes 'unmatched' count separately from 'skip_or_uncertain'
AC6: session_report.py counts UNMATCHED separately from UNCERTAIN and SKIP in compute_summary/console output
AC7: 0 behavioral criteria in tests/eval/scenarios/**/*.yaml hit the default UNMATCHED path — all existing criteria are covered by explicit branches
AC8: make validate passes with 0 errors
AC9: A regression test exists: synthetic criterion '__synthetic_unmatched__' produces UNMATCHED; known criterion 'No apologies in transcript' produces PASS unchanged
edge_cases: EC1: A scenario criterion that matches NO branch produces UNMATCHED, not PASS
EC2: Existing criteria that matched a branch before the change still produce the same verdict (PASS or UNCERTAIN) — no regression
EC3: The scoring formula treats UNMATCHED like UNCERTAIN — does not count as PASS in numerator
EC4: Trace vs no-trace paths: UNCERTAIN from heuristic non-match on traced sessions is distinct from UNMATCHED (never-matched criterion text)
verification_method: 1. Run audit script to verify 0 fallthrough criteria. 2. make validate. 3. Synthetic test: unmatched criterion → UNMATCHED, known criterion → unchanged. 4. session_judge.py --tier structural on a fixture with deliberate unmatched criterion.
